newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin orders sale of stakes in small oil firms.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin orders sale of stakes in small oil firms.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has signed a decree ordering the sale of state stakes in a host of smaller Russian oil companies, the presidential press service said on Monday.

A copy of the decree, obtained by Reuters, said that the companies affected included mini-major Tyumen Oil Company, regional oil firm KomiTEK and independent Norsi-Oil. The document gave no time frames, terms or stake sizes.
The other companies named were Vostsibneftegaz, the Eastern Oil Company (Vostochnaya Neftyanyaya Kompaniya) and SIBUR (Sibirsko-Uralskaya Neftegazokhimicheskaya Kompaniya).
Russia has sold off many large stakes in its new oil companies, both large and small, in the past two or so years, and has turned the once-state run sector into one of the country's most privatised.
KomiTEK's main operating unit is Komineft.
